proposals.announcement_evidence: This contract provides for tasks necessary to develop, field, and sustain Air Force Special Operations Command and Air Combat Command MQ-9 software development.
proposals.rationale: The announcement names the MQ-9 as the subject of the development work itself, not as a platform some other service supports: the order buys development, fielding and sustainment of MQ-9 software. Normalising the designator, "MQ-9" is the index row "MQ-9 UAV" with its generic type suffix dropped, and 0205219F is the MQ-9 program element itself — a program-named line, not a rollup or catch-all title. Money and mission agree: the announcement obligates "Fiscal 2017 and 2018 research and development funds in the amount of $9,864,489" against a cost-plus-fixed-fee order placed by Air Force Life Cycle Management Center, i.e. RDT&E dollars on an RDT&E operational-system-development line that funds precisely MQ-9 software. The only same-name collision in this org's index is "MQ-9 Mods" (PRDTB2, doc 407, procurement), which the R&D appropriation excludes; "MQ-9 System Lifecycle Agile Modernization (SLAM)" sits under this same 0205219F, so it creates no cross-PE ambiguity.

refute_a.reason: Money and mission both sit on this line: fiscal 2017/2018 research and development funds ($9,864,489) on a CPFF order placed by AFLCMC for MQ-9 software development itself, against the MQ-9's own RDT&E line (0205219F carried $167.2M FY17 and $184.4M FY18 actuals, and its FY26 narratives include MQ-9 Upgrade, MQ-9 SLAM and Squadron Operations Center software content), so the MQ-9 is the funded program rather than a platform the contract merely supports, and "MQ-9 UAV" is a program-named line, not a rollup or catch-all.

refute_b.reason: "MQ-9 UAV" is owned by 0205219F alone (the only other 0205219F row, MQ-9 SLAM, is the same PE); the one cross-PE MQ-9 name in the index is "MQ-9 Mods" (PRDTB2, doc 407), a distinct modifications name that the announcement's own "research and development funds" and software-development content do not fit, so the evidence does not link this award equally well there, the designator is real rather than invented, no MQ-9 variant or increment is named, and the quoted evidence is the work description, not the contractor.

proposals.announcement_evidence: systems engineering, technical assistance support, training, and development in performing integration, sustaining engineering and program management support functions for the Minuteman III weapon system
proposals.rationale: A real program name is present — Minuteman III is the LGM-30G the index carries under 0101213F — so this is not a phantom alias, but the evidence does not reach §1's standard for saying this action paid for that line's own work. What is bought is systems engineering and technical assistance, sustaining engineering and program management support, which §3 lists among generic services (engineering support), and the announcement obligates "Fiscal 2015 operations and maintenance and research and development funds in the amount of $16,723,542" — a mixed O&M/RDT&E obligation, and O&M sustainment attached to an RDT&E line is the failure mode the held-out study found. The name also collides across this org's own index: "LGM-30G" appears under both 0101213F (doc 412, Minuteman Squadrons) and M30MLG (doc 410, MM III Modifications), and nothing in the text resolves which of the two the money belongs to. Weak, not link.

proposals.announcement_evidence: the Joint Air-to-Surface Standoff Missile Group One development

proposals.rationale: The announcement spells the program's full name out verbatim — "the Joint Air-to-Surface Standoff Missile Group One development" — matching the index row under 0207325F apart from the leading article and the parenthetical acronym, so the name is the program itself and not a platform the contract merely supports. The work named is the program's own development content: "risk reduction testing, cyber testing and coatings to support the Group One development effort." The money agrees with the line: "Fiscal 2020 research, development, test and funds in the amount of $5,338,074" on a cost-plus-incentive-fee/cost-plus-fixed-fee development modification, i.e. RDT&E dollars against the JASSM RDT&E program element, whose title names the program rather than a catch-all. The only other JASSM-family row in this org's index is "AGM-158D" under JASSM0 (doc 410, procurement); the announcement names no AGM-158 variant and the obligation is RDT&E, so the procurement line is not the owner.

refute_a.reason: A development modification to the JASSM development contract for the program's own Group One development work (risk reduction testing, cyber testing, coatings) funded with fiscal 2020 RDT&E ($5,338,074) on the JASSM RDT&E line, which carried $73.5M in FY2020 actuals and whose narratives cover exactly this content ("Advanced Survivability, Integration, and Test"); the smaller fiscal 2019 other-procurement tranche is a secondary color that does not displace the RDT&E match, the missile is the program not a supported platform, and the line's title names the program.

refute_b.reason: "The Joint Air-to-Surface Standoff Missile (JASSM)" is a unique name row in the index, held only by 0207325F, which also owns AGM-158A/B/D and JASSM-ER; the procurement line JASSM0 owns only the variant name "AGM-158D" and LRASM0 only "AGM-158C", neither of which the announcement names, and "Group One" is a grouping inside the JASSM development effort rather than a separate indexed program, so no alternative owner fits this evidence.

proposals.program_name: Analytical Framework for Simulation Integration and Modeling (AFSIM)
proposals.announcement_evidence: This contract involves research, development, and expansion of the advanced framework for simulation, integration, and modeling, which is a modular, object-oriented multi-domain operations modeling, simulation, and analysis framework.
proposals.lexicon_quote: "Analytical Framework for Simulation Integration and Modeling (AFSIM)" (program_title: "Air Force Studies and Analysis Agency")
proposals.rationale: The announcement never writes the acronym, but it spells the program out: "the advanced framework for simulation, integration, and modeling" is AFSIM, differing from the index row's expansion only in the first word, and the announcement's own gloss — "a modular, object-oriented multi-domain operations modeling, simulation, and analysis framework" — is AFSIM's standing description, which is why this is an alias match rather than a coincidence of common words. The named thing is a software framework, so there is no platform-versus-program confusion, and the line's work is exactly what is bought: "completing research and development for redefining the basic analytical and simulation environment (REBASE)" is R&D on that framework. The appropriation agrees — the initial task orders are "Foundation I research and development" and "Expansion I research and development", RDT&E content against an RDT&E program element (doc 412). 0901226F is the only PE in this org's index that owns any AFSIM-shaped name, so there is no competing owner; its title names the owning analysis agency rather than a catch-all dollar threshold.

refute_a.reason: The money cannot be this line's: Air Force Research Laboratory awarded the REBASE IDIQ and the single FY2021 RDT&E obligation of $2,800,000 is more than double 0901226F's entire FY2021 actual of $1.151M (the PE runs $0.87M-$1.5M a year through FY2024 and only reaches $9.9M/$14.8M in FY2025/26, which is the edition whose narrative owns the AFSIM name), so a $48M AFRL ceiling in 2021 was funded by AFRL's own RDT&E lines; 0901226F is in any case an agency-titled management-support M&S studies line — a rollup of the analysis agency's model portfolio (AFSIM, STORM, AD-ARM, Joint M&S Gateway) — not the program element that bought this development.

refute_b.reason: The alias is real, not invented — "advanced framework for simulation, integration, and modeling" is the standing alternate expansion of AFSIM and the announcement's own gloss is AFSIM's canonical description — and AFSIM appears exactly once in the whole index, under 0901226F; every other modeling/simulation row (JSE across six PEs, STORM under this same PE, CAVE, DMOC Replay Tool, C2SET, WIE) carries a different program name that this evidence does not fit, so there is no competing owner and no variant/increment confusion.
